title: LEADERG's “AI door god” camera analytics at Beigang Wude Temple flags smoke in an empty office a minute before charging lithium batteries burst; the night clerk and Yunlin firefighters hold the 5 February 2026 fire to ten square meters, nobody hurt, main hall untouched
summary: AI camera analytics flagged smoke in an empty temple office a minute before a battery fire; held to 10 m², no injuries, main hall intact.
account: At about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 the AI門神 (AI door god) system flagged smoke in a first-floor office and machine room, empty after hours. The system is run by 立達軟體 (LEADERG Inc.) over the closed-circuit television (CCTV) of Beigang Wude Temple, Yunlin County, Taiwan. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and chairman 林安樂, in Japan, by LINE. The night-duty clerk reached the room with an extinguisher within a minute. At 05:33 overheated lithium batteries beside a tool charger burst and flames spread. Staff called 119 at 05:36. Yunlin County Fire Bureau crews arrived at 05:44, controlled it at 06:10 and put it out at 06:14. Ten square meters burned. Nobody was hurt. The main hall and statues were untouched.
purpose: AI門神 (“AI door god: temple AI fire-and-theft prevention system”) was built to run AI image recognition over a temple's existing CCTV. It was built to detect excess smoke, flame and suspicious behavior, and to alert staff by SMS, LINE or email. CTS reported in December 2024 that Wude Temple's door-god system would sound an alarm at once on abnormal smoke. Flagging smoke before a fire was exactly its designed purpose.
system: AI門神：宮廟AI防火防盜系統 (AI Door God: temple AI fire-and-theft prevention system), AI image recognition over the temple's existing CCTV with alerts by SMS, LINE and email
model_version: Not named. Advantech's case study says the image-recognition algorithms were developed with a large language model as the basis and run on an Advantech IPC-730 with a SKY-QUAD-5000A-32 accelerator card at about five seconds per frame.
developer: 立達軟體科技股份有限公司 (LEADERG Inc.), Taiwan
segment: Temple and cultural-asset protection: AI video analytics on existing CCTV
taxonomy_note: Fire spread averted is read as reduced potential for harm; Trustible's description stresses legal harm.

ratings.reason: The temple's loss was the contents of one first-floor office of about ten square meters (staff lockers, some tea, sweets, incense and joss paper). The main hall, statues and worship areas were untouched. The temple stayed open in the run-up to the Lunar New Year crowds. The fire bureau credited the reinforced-concrete structure and its own eight-minute arrival for the containment. A conventional smoke alarm sounded as well. So the share attributable to the AI alert is a minute or two of earlier warning, not the whole saved building.

ai_role.statement: The system's documented contribution is the first alert. By the temple's own log it detected smoke at 05:30, a minute before the lithium batteries burst at 05:33. It messaged the front desk, the general manager and the chairman in sequence over LINE. That is how a chairman asleep in Nara came to follow the fire on the temple's cameras. The suppression was human. The clerk's extinguisher failed once the batteries burst. The Yunlin County Fire Bureau's eight trucks and eighteen firefighters, called at 05:36, controlled the fire at 06:10. UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well. The Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 attributed the containment to the building's reinforced-concrete structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. The LINE relay from the vendor is the chairman's account, not the bureau's.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. The Monitor's date of 4 February is the UTC date; every source puts the fire at about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 Taiwan time (21:30 UTC on 4 February), so the date observed is 5 February. Times differ between the temple's log (fire controlled 05:51) and the fire bureau (controlled 06:10, extinguished 06:14); the record uses the bureau's. The CTS broadcast report of 5 February and CTS's December 2024 piece on the door-god system were found through Brave, as WebSearch was exhausted; DuckDuckGo and Mojeek returned nothing. The chairman's Facebook post was not read; it is quoted by UDN, NOWnews and NextApple. No Yunlin County Fire Bureau release was found on its own site; its statements are quoted by 觀傳媒, 台灣好報 and 創新聞, and CTS quotes the Beigang sub-station chief 陳思淵. revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented: the protective action (a smoke alert at 05:30, a minute before the batteries burst, relayed over LINE to the front desk, general manager and chairman) is documented by the temple's own timeline as reported by TVBS, UDN, NOWnews, 觀傳媒 and CTS, and the outcome by the Yunlin County Fire Bureau's figures, but the counterfactual is not shown: UDN reports that a residential smoke alarm (住警器) sounded as well, a clerk was on night duty in any case, and the Third Brigade commander 陳岳謄 credited the RC structure and the crews' quick arrival without mentioning the AI. The Monitor's date of 4 February is the UTC date; every source puts the fire at about 05:30 on 5 February 2026 Taiwan time (21:30 UTC on 4 February), so the date observed is 5 February. Times differ between the temple's log (fire controlled 05:51) and the fire bureau (controlled 06:10, extinguished 06:14); the record uses the bureau's. The cause (a tool charger and lithium batteries) is the chairman's account; UDN's first report says the bureau was still investigating and the secretary general 蘇建華 told TVBS he suspected wiring. The vendor is named by the chairman as 立達軟體; its identity as LEADERG Inc. and the system's design (AI image recognition over existing CCTV on Advantech hardware, alerts by SMS, LINE or email, deployed at Wude Temple) come from Advantech's April 2025 case study, which is partner-authored and used only as an additional source. The chairman's Facebook post was not read; it is quoted by UDN, NOWnews and NextApple. No Yunlin County Fire Bureau release was found on its own site; its statements are quoted by 觀傳媒, 台灣好報 and 創新聞, and CTS quotes the Beigang sub-station chief 陳思淵.
